title: Haitian TPS Holders in the US Describe Fear and Disruption as Status Termination Takes Hold
detail: An NPR/member-station report published September 15, 2026 documented the fallout in Haitian-American communities — Miami's Little Haiti, North Lauderdale, and Springfield, Ohio — after roughly 350,000 Haitian nationals lost Temporary Protected Status when termination took effect in late July 2026, ending 16 years of deportation protection. A North Lauderdale church's adult English-learning program saw enrollment fall from 231 to 17 students, and at least 14 parishioners have been detained by immigration officers. A registered nurse who lost her TPS described living in fear: 'You would think I was on the run. Who am I on the run from?' A religious leader said the community was 'being deconstructed completely.' The report ties the disruption directly to conditions inside Haiti, where gang control of the capital and recent massacres — including the killing of civilians inside a Kenscoff church — make return dangerous for those who lose status and face deportation.
